text:
adele: kicking off a short thread to align on the PRD scope for Reserved GPU pools SLA + autoscale. want to capture acceptance criteria, sizing heuristics, and failure modes before i write the doc.

samir: SGTM. i can sketch throughput math and an initial autoscale policy.

maria: will need clear SLOs for p99 latency and burst behavior to map to oncall/escapes.

chad: customer asks: predictable p95 < 150ms for gen routes, plus tail protection when noisy tenants spike. also request graceful degraded mode to cheaper models.

adele: notes i'm thinking of including three concrete SLA tiers: Bronze (best-effort), Silver (backed by reserved pool), Gold (reserved + preemptive warm capacity). thoughts?

samir: suggest we avoid vague names — map to numbers: Bronze = 99.5 p95, Silver = 99.9 p95, Gold = 99.95 p95. tie to throughput per GPU and cold start windows.

jun: agreed. also call out admission control: reject vs queue. we need queue timeout policy.

olivia: ops ask: define overload fallback chain: queue -> throttle -> degrade -> reject. need metrics for each step.

maria: edge case: multi-tenant shoppers where one tenant uses bursty batch embedding calls and starves gen traffic. plan: tenant-level circuit breaker + fair-share token bucket.

samir: here is quick math for throughput. assuming A100-80GB ~ 120 tokens/s for model-x at avg 32-token request: 3.75 req/s per GPU. with batching 2x -> ~7.5 req/s. so 1k rps needs ~134 GPUs raw, add 20% headroom = 161.

adele: can you add an appendix with sample calc and assumptions in PRD? i'll link to it.

samir: will do. also want autoscale rules draft:
```
- scale up: when 3min avg utilization > 70% or queue depth > 50 requests for 2 consecutive minutes
- scale down: when 10min avg utilization < 40% and queue depth == 0
- cool-down: 5min between scale ops
- min_pool: commit size by tier (Gold=8 GPUs, Silver=4, Bronze=0)
```

chad: need acceptance criteria for launch. propose:
```
- functional: reserved pools can be created, updated, deleted via console/API
- performance: for Silver/Gal, p95 gen latency meets SLA under steady load for 1 hour test
- autoscale: during synthetic spike, pool scales up within target time and scales down without thrash
- degradation: fallback to cheaper model occurs and consumer gets a clear error code/metric
- observability: dashboard shows per-pool p95/p99, queue depth, scaling events, tenant fairness metric
```

adele: good start. add edge-case acceptance: region failover (traffic routed to secondary region within 30s and honoring tier where capacity exists) and capacity oversubscription behavior documented.

maria: question: do we guarantee cross-region FIFO ordering? probably not — we should explicitly call out ordering tradeoffs for failover.

olivia: agree, state ordering is not guaranteed on failover and app teams must be prepared.

samir: autoscale stability: we should add a canary rollout step in PRD: enable autoscale on 10% of pools for 48h with increased metrics retention.

chad: acceptance for canary: no >5% error rate increase, no >15% p95 regressions for canary customers.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: ops/canary-autoscale at 2026-06-10T03:00Z (placeholder) :rocket:

adele: next actions:
- samir: drop the throughput appendix + autoscale rules into a PRD draft by EOD Wed
- maria: add SRE playbook bullets for overload, circuit breaker, and region failover by Thu
- olivia: mockups for console pool UI and observability page by Fri
- chad: compile customer asks doc and map to SLA tiers by Thu

samir: i can also include a CLI/API schema snippet. example: `POST /reserved_pools {"name":"gold-east-1","tier":"Gold","min_gpus":8}`

adele: perfect. i'll assemble and ping this channel for review. want to keep the PRD concise (1-2 pages + appendices).

jun: small note — include a short section on billing implications (committed vs burst usage) so finance doesn't get surprised.

adele: noted. thanks everyone — will draft and start a formal RFC link when ready.

olivia: thumbs up :thumbsup:

chad: thanks, will review once draft is up.

samir: will upload math + a csv of sample sizing numbers to the PRD draft.

adele: closing loop: target RFC publish next Tue for stakeholder feedback. if blockers surface earlier, callout ASAP.
